mappings.title: FR-10 `auditing-skills` reverse-check posture (OI-R2a-2)

options.name: separate_parallel_rule_in_auditing_skills
options.description: Author a new reverse-check rule inside `.claude/skills/auditing-skills/` mirroring FR-10's matrix-presence predicate at the skill-side. When a new skill is authored, the rule checks whether agents whose `skills:` arrays should include it actually do. One small rule file; one new audit dimension.
pros: Separation of concerns: auditing-subagents covers agent-side matrix presence (FR-10's existing scope); auditing-skills covers skill-side `skills:`-array completeness — each audit family stays internally coherent.
Low blast radius (one new rule file under one skill family).
Two-way reversible — rule can be relaxed or removed if the audit gap doesn't materialize.
Discoverability: skill-side audit findings surface under the skill-side skill, which is where authors look for skill-related issues.
cons: Single-sourced supporting claim (C-0072 in R2a corpus); investigation deferred this run rather than researched.
Two audit families end up with structurally-similar rules; manual sync risk if either evolves.
Externally undecided (no T-corroborator in R2a corpus).
preconditions: New rule entry in `.claude/skills/auditing-skills/SKILL.md` mirroring the FR-10 predicate shape at the skill level.
Predicate scoped to: 'when a new skill file is authored, audit whether existing agents whose load-rules indicate they should load it actually have it in `skills:`'.
options.parent_alignment: Matches parent's D-3 lean (separate rule on auditing-skills, weak strength). R2a re-affirms because the audit-family symmetry argument still applies and codebase facts (parent C-0091: auditing-skills carries its own conventions) are unchanged.

options.name: fold_into_fr10_auditing_subagents_rule
options.description: Extend FR-10's auditing-subagents rule predicate to also enumerate auditing-skills targets. One rule, two surfaces.
pros: Single rule definition; no cross-family sync risk.
Simpler PRD-level traceability.
cons: Conflates two audit dimensions (matrix presence vs skill-array completeness) — undermines FR-10's narrow scope.
Couples two audit families to one rule change cadence — auditing-skills inherits auditing-subagents schema changes unintentionally.
PRD policy explicitly carries OI-R2a-2 as Blueprint Open Question rather than folding (PRD §Product Policy); this option fights that policy.
evidence_anchors: C-0072 (deferred); parent C-0123 (FR-10's current narrow scope)
options.rejection_rationale: Conflates two audit dimensions PRD policy explicitly keeps separate. The two-way-reversibility argument does not save it because the FR-10 scope already shipped narrowly in parent.

options.name: defer_to_future_feature
options.description: Decline to add the reverse-check in R2a; document why not (close OI-R2a-2). Revisit only if a real audit gap surfaces in practice.
pros: Lowest immediate cost; honest about externally-undecided status.
Consistent with PRD §O event-triggered posture.
cons: Leaves an asymmetric audit surface in the meantime.
Adds another deferral to the register, which competes with FR-11's goal (replace post-ship felt-utility with event-triggered triggers — adding deferrals can become its own ritual).
Contradicts the parent's lean toward the separate rule (which was the lean R2a is asked to re-affirm).
preconditions: Deferral entry in issue register documenting why not.
options.rejection_rationale: Acceptable fallback but contradicts parent lean R2a is re-affirming. Deferring the audit-family symmetry indefinitely undermines the cumulative discipline FR-10 establishes.

mappings.rationale: Re-affirms parent's lean. Symmetric audit surfaces; low cost; reversible. The single-sourced status (C-0072) is acknowledged but the codebase facts (audit-family separation is the existing pattern) make this the lowest-risk path forward. Blueprint may downgrade to defer if the Composer judges the audit gap unlikely to materialize.

mappings.title: FR-9 Blocks-X marker grammar canonicalization
mappings.summary_paragraph: Closed in the parent run by ADR-0063. R2a inherits the canonical grammar `<!-- BLOCKS: <stage-slug>-completion -->` (uppercase token, colon-suffixed, HTML-comment container, optional `\u2014`-separated payload, parser regex `<!--\s*BLOCKS:\s*([a-z0-9-]+)-completion(?:\s+\u2014\s+[^\n]*)?\s*-->`) per ADR-0063's Decision Details section. The grammar was selected because n=1 prior prose occurrence is not a grammar to honor and structured pragmas are greppable from CI, invisible in rendered markdown, and multi-slug-ready. Non-retroactive migration: the n=1 prior occurrence at `working/feature/devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1/codebase-analysis-report.md:198-202` is not migrated. R2a authors realization concerns (parser placement decided separately under D-R2a-3); the grammar question itself is settled. Anchoring evidence in corpus: C-0026, C-0027, C-0028, C-0029, C-0030, C-0085, C-0088.

mappings.title: FR-6 trigger conditions 3 & 4 mechanical evaluator (OI-R2a-1)

options.name: hybrid_advisory_mechanical_predicate_with_human_ratification
options.description: A mechanical predicate scans Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions table (FR-7's output) for trigger-shaped tokens: trigger 3 ('new skill that the feature's design indicates one or more existing agents will load' — predicate checks 'dogfood_decision' column for new-skill values cross-referenced against agents named in adjacent rows); trigger 4 ('new domain concept whose skill-coverage decision names an existing agent as a downstream consumer' — predicate checks for agent-name tokens in the 'covering-agent' or 'consumer' column). The predicate surfaces an advisory annotation at the Design Composition gate; design-composer (human) ratifies whether FR-6 matrix is required. Override events log to state-transitions.log for retrospective tuning.
pros: FR-7 table is mechanically parseable per codebase researcher (C-0071) — HIGH suitability for the predicate route.
Balances mechanical determinism with human judgment on interpretive triggers.
Couples cleanly with D-8 (substance-not-presence heuristic) — predicate checks shape, human checks substance.
Logged overrides allow predicate tuning: high false-negative rate → tighten; low → promote to mandatory.
Cheap to ship; cheap to tune; two-way reversible.
cons: Two-system maintenance (predicate code + human-checklist).
Externally undecided in R2a corpus — relies on parent's lean and inspectable codebase facts.
Risk of human ratification becoming a rubber stamp if predicate is over-trusted.
evidence_anchors: C-0071 (FR-7 table mechanically parseable — HIGH suitability)
C-0082 (Design Composition gate as ratification surface)
preconditions: Predicate hosted in `.claude/skills/auditing-subagents/scripts/` (consistent with FR-10's rule realization under D-R2a-5).
`design-composer.md` procedure has a ratification step at Design Composition gate.
State-transitions.log entry shape extended for override events (auditing-shared/log_state_transition.py).
FR-7 table shape stable (concept | covering-skill | confidence | dogfood-decision | rationale) before predicate authoring.

cost.runtime_overhead: minor (one grep + one human checkpoint per Design Composition gate)

options.parent_alignment: Re-affirms parent's hybrid lean. R2a strengthens the recommendation because C-0071 (FR-7 table mechanically parseable) is fresh codebase evidence supporting the predicate component.

options.name: full_machine_checkable_predicate_only
options.description: Deterministic predicate over Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions table gates the matrix-mandatory check with no human checkpoint. Triggers 3 and 4 evaluated by token-pattern match against the table cells.
pros: Deterministic; auditable; fastest gate (no human-in-loop).
If FR-7 table substance is high-quality, false-negative rate is low.
cons: Triggers 3 and 4 are interpretive — pattern-match brittleness yields false negatives when authors phrase 'cross-skill impact' or 'downstream consumer' in different ways.
Conflicts with D-8's substance-not-presence heuristic — predicate checks presence-of-phrasing, not substance-of-intent.
Single point of failure: a missed trigger is silently un-audited.

Even with high FR-7 table quality (C-0071), trigger 4's 'names an existing agent' is parseable but trigger 3's 'design indicates one or more existing agents will load' requires interpretive read of design context the table cell may not capture.
options.rejection_rationale: Interpretive triggers do not survive predicate-only enforcement; symmetric to T-003's anti-ritualism trade-off — checking phrasing is presence-not-substance.

options.name: human_in_loop_checkpoint_only
options.description: design-composer (human) checks Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions at Design Composition gate; no mechanical evaluator. Trigger 3 and 4 are judgment calls every time.
pros: Highest signal fidelity on interpretive triggers.
No false-negative chase; no maintenance burden on a predicate.
Coheres with FR-7's substance-not-presence framing.
cons: Highest ritual cost — every Design Composition repeats the full check.
No advisory annotation to focus reviewer attention; reviewer reads the whole section every time.
Inconsistent application across runs (reviewer-dependent).
Waste FR-7 table's mechanical parseability (C-0071) — passes up free signal.
evidence_anchors: C-0082 (Design Composition gate is the human checkpoint surface today)
options.rejection_rationale: Wastes the table's mechanical parseability surfaced by C-0071. The advisory predicate is cheap and directly reduces reviewer load without claiming authoritative judgment.

mappings.rationale: Re-affirms parent's hybrid lean. Predicate-only loses signal on interpretive triggers; human-only wastes reviewer attention on shape-checks the machine can pre-filter. The hybrid pairs cheap pre-screening with authoritative human ratification and logs overrides for tuning. C-0071 (R2a-fresh codebase evidence) strengthens the predicate-feasibility argument.
mappings.cross_decision_dependency: Couples to D-8 (substance-not-presence heuristic). The predicate here MUST NOT score substance; it scores shape only.

mappings.title: FR-7 W/H/A trifecta — substance heuristic vs structural mandate
mappings.graph_note: Heaviest node in graph (E-0003 FR-7 with 23 claim back-pointers). Decision is the most consequential R2a architectural choice; framing choice ripples through FR-7 ACs, dogfood deliverable validation, and downstream consumer expectations.

options.name: hybrid_mandate_for_new_skill_proposals_substance_heuristic_for_existing_skill_rows
options.description: W/H/A is the substance reviewers check for (need-justification / scope-lifecycle hygiene / anti-pattern defenses per T-003's 3-category convergence). Reviewers apply a substance-not-presence heuristic: the trifecta is satisfied if the substance is present, regardless of whether three labelled headings exist. EXCEPTION: when a Skill-Coverage Decision row proposes a NEW skill (dogfood_decision = 'propose-new-skill'), a structured W/H/A artifact with three labelled headings is mandated. For 'existing-skill' rows and 'no-skill-warranted' rows, the substance principle governs.
pros: Preserves T-003's cross-platform-convergent substance (6 platforms verified) without inheriting the novel-ritualism risk (C-0257 identifies codification-as-mandate as the novel and risky move).
Reviewer cost is lowered exactly where it's highest (new-skill proposals are the most expensive review surface — they introduce ongoing maintenance debt).
Substance heuristic aligns with how reviewers actually catch missing rationale — substance-checking, not heading-counting.
Coheres with D-5's advisory-predicate design (machine checks shape; human checks substance).

Graph structural-novelty observation reinforces hybrid: FR-7 is the heaviest node (23 back-pointers), confirming codification-as-artifact is novel and warrants explicit risk-mitigation via the substance heuristic rather than open-ended mandate.
cons: Substance heuristic is harder to mechanically evaluate — reviewer-dependent.

Drawing the new-skill-proposal boundary requires a clear definition (likely: 'dogfood_decision row indicates a propose-new-skill resolution, OR the row creates a new directory under `.claude/skills/`').
Quantitative BFCL evidence is directional (C-0184), not a measured threshold for this pipeline.
Skill-coverage decision codification is novel (genesis stage per framer) — no production precedent for the exact shape.
evidence_anchors: C-0190 / C-0192 / C-0193 / C-0194 (T-003 cross-platform W/H/A convergence)
C-0257 (codification-as-mandate is the novel move; ritualism risk)
preconditions: KB-cc-design hosts the W/H/A rubric + substance heuristic.
FR-7 section template extended with three labelled headings (Why / How / Anti-patterns) for new-skill rows.
'New skill proposal' boundary defined in FR-7 template instructions.
design-composer.md procedure references the rubric at skill-coverage decision time.

cost.irreversibility_cost: low (two-way; relax to principle-only or tighten to universal-mandate later)

options.parent_alignment: Re-affirms parent's hybrid lean. R2a strengthens with graph structural-novelty observation: heaviest-node status (23 back-pointers) corroborates the parent's gloss that codification-as-artifact is the novel move warranting risk-mitigation.

options.name: full_structural_mandate_universally
options.description: Every Skill-Coverage Decision row MUST produce a structured W/H/A artifact with three labelled headings — regardless of dogfood_decision resolution type. Reviewer checks presence; auditor checks each row has three non-empty cells.
pros: Maximum auditability — mechanically gateable (does each row have three populated cells?).
Removes reviewer judgment on shape.
Easiest predicate for FR-10 audit (matrix-cell-population check).
cons: 0/6 surveyed platforms mandate this (C-0257) — novel-ritualism risk explicitly identified by T-003.
Presence-not-substance: three filled headings can be empty of meaningful content and still pass the gate (the exact failure mode FR-7 is designed to prevent).
Drives authors toward ritualistic minimum-viable filings on existing-skill rows where the substance is already well-trodden community ground, undermining the actual goal.
PRD §Product Policy already codifies 'substance over form' — universal mandate fights that policy.

cost.irreversibility_cost: moderate (relaxing a mandate is harder than tightening a principle)

options.rejection_rationale: T-003 explicitly identifies codification-as-mandate as the novel and risky move; 0/6 surveyed platforms mandate. The recommended hybrid captures substance without the ritual. PRD policy alignment seals it.

options.name: principle_with_substance_heuristic_only_no_mandate
options.description: W/H/A is a principle in KB-cc-design; reviewers apply substance heuristic to ALL skill-coverage decisions including new-skill proposals. No mandate anywhere; no required template headings.
pros: Lightest authorial burden.
Maximum substance preservation (zero ritual).
Cleanest alignment with 'substance over form' PRD policy.
cons: Loses the audit anchor for new-skill proposals — the most expensive review surface gets the least structure.
Higher reviewer cognitive load on new-skill proposals where structure pays for itself.
Drift risk: principle without occasional structured artifact tends to fade in practice.
No mechanical gate available for D-5's predicate to leverage when checking trigger 3 (new-skill triggering matrix-mandatory).
options.rejection_rationale: Defensible but loses the new-skill-proposal carve-out where structure pays for itself. The hybrid is the principled middle path; pure principle-only sacrifices a useful audit anchor for marginal additional substance-preservation.

mappings.rationale: Re-affirms parent's hybrid lean with R2a graph-structural-novelty observation. The hybrid preserves T-003 cross-source-convergent substance; respects the documented anti-ritualism trade-off; concentrates structural mandate where it has the highest review-cost ROI (new-skill proposals). The 23-back-pointer heaviest-node status of FR-7 in the R2a graph corroborates the parent's framing that the codification-as-artifact is the novel move — explicit risk-mitigation via substance heuristic is the rational response. Couples cleanly with D-5's predicate-checks-shape / human-checks-substance split.
loss_summary: pattern_fidelity: none (substance preserved across the cross-platform convergence)
mappings.cross_decision_dependency: Couples to D-5 (the advisory predicate there scores shape, not substance). Coupling is explicit and load-bearing: D-5's predicate trigger 3/4 evaluation MUST defer to the substance heuristic articulated here.

mappings.title: Severity-vocabulary bridge content (ADR-0061 host inherited; R2a authors content)
mappings.closure_pointer: Host decided by inherited ADR-0061 (canonical host `.claude/skills/KB-review-disciplines/references/severity-taxonomy.md`). R2a authors the bridge CONTENT.

bridge_mapping_shape.purpose: The bridge maps three audience-specific severity vocabularies into a single reference without collapsing audience-fit. It additionally preserves two distinct severity-weight sets (verdict-compute weights AND iteration-delta weights) that conflict_with each other and therefore MUST NOT be collapsed.
bridge_mapping_shape.structural_form: Markdown table with 5 columns (3 vocab columns + 1 non-monotonic-edge column + 1 iteration-delta-weight column) plus an explicit Weight Preservation Note section.

table_columns.additional_blocker_penalty: BLOCKER applies its -12 plus an additional -12 flat penalty per occurrence (24 total per BLOCKER). Source: verdict_compute.py:97, :158-160.
table_columns.intra_auditor_divergence_note: review-architecture-auditor.md + review-cross-artifact-auditor.md emit BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/INFO (no NIT); auditing-mcp SKILL.md uses BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT (no INFO). verdict_compute.py is the canonical union: BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT/INFO.

definitions.critical: Issue blocks acceptance. Architecturally wrong, security-breaking, contract violation, or fundamentally infeasible. Cannot be deferred or accepted with conditions \u2014 must be fixed.
definitions.important: Issue should be fixed before approval but isn't architecturally fatal. Degrades score. Can be deferred only with explicit user approval + tracked ledger entry.
definitions.recommended: Improvement suggestion. Non-blocking. Documents are approvable with `recommended` issues outstanding.

table_columns.source_file: .claude/skills/KB-review-disciplines/references/severity-taxonomy.md (pre-bridge content; bridge author appends bridge sections additively per OI-R2a-6)

table_columns.note: Inlined in agent prompt (per parent Known Issue 3); not in a separate KB file.

table_columns.purpose: Captures cross-vocab mappings that are not strictly monotonic, with explicit rationale fields per edge. Bridge MUST surface (not collapse) these.

documented_edges.reviewer_recommended: non-blocking improvement; documents approvable with recommended outstanding
documented_edges.translation_difficulty: NIT carries 'taste' framing (subjective); recommended carries 'improvement' framing (actionable). Auditor NIT often safely \u2192 recommended, but reverse mapping (recommended \u2192 NIT) loses actionability. Optional translator (auditing-shared/scripts/translate_severity.py) surfaces 'taste-vs-improvement' as an explicit rationale field.

documented_edges.auditor_MAJOR: should be fixed before approval; -5 weight; conditional_pass verdict if no BLOCKER
documented_edges.pv_blocking_vs_warning: blocking = gate refuses to advance; warning = gate advances with note. MAJOR \u2192 branch depends on whether PV's invariant is itself blocking-class (per FR-3 R2b).
documented_edges.translation_rule: default MAJOR \u2192 blocking; downgrade to warning only with explicit per-finding rationale stating why the PV-tier invariant is non-blocking.

documented_edges.verdict_compute_canonical: supports both NIT (-0.5) and INFO (0) as distinct values
documented_edges.bridge_recommendation: preserve both; document NIT for taste/style and INFO for neutral observations (different intent). This is parent's Known Issue 2 \u2014 documented rather than collapsed.

table_columns.purpose: Preserves the SECOND severity-weight set used for review-iteration delta math, which conflicts with verdict-compute weights and MUST NOT be collapsed.
table_columns.conflict_with_verdict_compute_weights: verdict_compute.py uses {BLOCKER: -12, MAJOR: -5, MINOR: -2, NIT: -0.5, INFO: 0} for absolute verdict scoring; review-cross-artifact-auditor uses {BLOCKER: 10, MAJOR: 3, MINOR: 1, INFO: 0} for iteration-delta change-detection. Different mathematical roles; both must remain. The R2a graph surfaces this as a `conflicts_with` edge (E-0049 \u2194 E-0046) that the bridge content MUST document, not collapse.

weight_preservation_note.title: Two Weight Sets \u2014 Why Both Remain
weight_preservation_note.content: The bridge documents TWO distinct severity-weight mappings because they serve different mathematical roles: (1) verdict-compute weights (-12 / -5 / -2 / -0.5 / 0) drive absolute verdict scoring in verdict_compute.py \u2014 they answer 'is this audit a PASS?'; (2) iteration-delta weights (10 / 3 / 1 / 0) drive severity-weighted count deltas across review iterations in review-cross-artifact-auditor.md:93 \u2014 they answer 'did this iteration improve relative to the previous?'. Collapsing to one weight set would silently break the iteration-delta math (the inverse-sign relationship between absolute scoring and delta improvement is load-bearing). Documented, not reconciled. R2a graph edge: E-0049 conflicts_with E-0046 (claims C-0042, C-0043, C-0092, C-0094) \u2014 surfaced explicitly here per the framer's note that 'collapsing would silently break iteration-delta verdict math'.

nfr8_four_field_shape_co_located.purpose: Per ADR-0061, the bridge host file also documents the NFR-8 four-field finding shape that downstream FR-1/9/10 emitters use.
nfr8_four_field_shape_co_located.delta_from_existing_audit_issues_json: NFR-8's four fields are NOT currently in audit-issues.json schema. design-composer adds these as new sub-fields under issues[] (additive). Parent's analysis confirmed schema-extension is structurally safe across the 12 known downstream consumers (codebase-analysis.json blast_radius_new_confirmations[2]).

monotonic_mappings_for_reference.note: Strictest tier in each vocabulary; consistent intent (gate-blocking).
Lowest non-zero severity; consistent intent (non-blocking but actionable).

bridge_mapping_shape.host_file_location: .claude/skills/KB-review-disciplines/references/severity-taxonomy.md (per ADR-0061). Additive to existing pre-bridge content (vocabulary definitions for critical/important/recommended, threshold mappings).
consumers: 20 agents load KB-review-disciplines (per codebase-analysis blast_radius_new_confirmations[4]) \u2014 bridge visible to all automatically; no separate propagation work.
FR-1 finding emitters (review-architecture-auditor) reference bridge by name per ADR-0061 Implementation Guidance ('reference by name, not by copy').
FR-9 marker handling (orchestrator gating) consults bridge for severity vocabulary when emitting Blocks-X resolution events.
FR-10 audit rule emission references bridge for severity assignment on matrix-missing findings.
R2b consumers (FR-4, FR-5) inherit the populated bridge.

evidence_anchors: C-0023 / C-0024 (NFR-8 four-field shape co-located per ADR-0061)
C-0042 / C-0043 (verdict_compute weights vs iteration-delta weights conflict — the load-bearing graph edge)
C-0056 / C-0057 / C-0058 (cross-vocab non-monotonic edge surface)
C-0079 / C-0080 (bridge sequencing — purely additive at HEAD, no collision)
C-0088 (cross-ADR references — ADR-0059, ADR-0061, ADR-0063 mutual)
C-0092 / C-0094 (Open Question #2 surfaces — both weight sets must be documented)
mappings.rationale: D-10 is content authoring, not option-choosing. The bridge mapping shape above is the substrate: a 5-column table (3 vocab + 1 non-monotonic edge + 1 iteration-delta weight) plus a Weight Preservation Note that documents both weight sets without collapsing them. The R2a graph's `conflicts_with` edge between E-0049 (iteration-delta weights) and E-0046 (verdict-compute weights) is load-bearing — collapsing would silently break iteration-delta verdict math. The 20-agent KB-review-disciplines consumer set means the bridge's correctness propagates broadly; design-composer's authoring discipline is the chokepoint. Non-monotonic edges are surfaced (not collapsed) per parent's Known Issue 2 resolution.
loss_summary: pattern_fidelity: none (each surface preserves its idiom; bridge is the translation reference)
mappings.deferred_to: design-composer (ratifies bridge wording at Design Composition gate — cross-cuts layers per parent's D-10 routing)
